method: Router 0x18e0a60 runs natively and tail-calls 0x18dfa10 with the found node index in r8d; 0x18dfa10, basis composition 0x18c16e0, append 0x18dccb0 and reserve 0x18df1e0 run natively. Python composes route_pose_flagged_pair_indexed with update_pose_flagged_neighbor.
comparisons: ordered supplied calls with every argument
both 12-float world transforms passed to the tester, bit-exact
tester factory and shape pointers in the query block
all fixture bytes: provider, owner, pair, tree nodes, records, entry arrays incl. stale slots, bodies, kinds, shape entries, local transforms, shapes, masks and new allocations
coverage: dormant pair (both inactive) with and without state-1 promotion
active via frame id and via kind+0x53 nibble
null first/second shape, non-solid first/second shape entry
different group (q masks), same group with kind+0x52&0x10 (d masks only) and without (both)
tester hit with new/existing entry, miss with/without entry removal
float32 specials: signed zero, subnormal inputs, products that underflow
failure_proof: Removing the stale entry when the second shape pointer is null fails at case 10 (entry-array bytes).
Ignoring the kind+0x52&0x10 same-group d-mask-only branch fails at case 31 (service log).
Adding the translation before the z term in the shape world translation fails at case 14 (tester world bits).
Treating either-inactive as dormant fails at case 10.
limits: Tester factory and overlap test are authored random stand-ins; no narrow-phase geometry is reconstructed.
Services do not mutate fixture memory, so reread order around tester calls is not discriminated.
Trees are authored unbalanced BSTs (search only); records, shapes and masks are synthetic.
Same-body pairs are included occasionally; whether the native producer emits them is unknown.
No NaN or overflow-to-infinity inputs (host default-NaN sign may differ from x86); no live validation.
